fixtures.rationale: loadRates awaits a bare fetch call with no timeout, abort signal, retry, or fallback anywhere in the body, so a hung or failed request hangs this function indefinitely.
listOrders awaits a database query with no timeout, retry, or circuit visible in the function, so a slow or dead pool hangs the caller.
charge awaits the Stripe SDK's charge creation directly with no timeout, retry, or fallback, so a Stripe outage fails this function with no design for it.
emit awaits a queue publish with no timeout, retry, or circuit, so a stalled broker hangs this function with no fallback.
loadRates awaits fetch with an AbortSignal timeout attached directly to the call, so the outbound call is covered by a visible timeout policy in this body.
loadRates's outbound call to client.get is awaited inside a retry wrapper whose options state the retry policy, so the call is covered rather than left unguarded.

The query is raced against a rejecting timer, so a hung database rejects this function after three seconds instead of hanging it. The parser marks only the outer Promise.race as awaited; the collector treats a call nested inside an awaited expression as awaited too, so pool.query is the outbound call and the Promise.race line is the resilience evidence.
loadRates awaits fetch inside a try whose catch and comment both name the fallback path, so the outbound call is covered by a documented fallback rather than left unguarded.
double is pure computation with no calls at all, so there is no outbound evidence and no candidate.

loadRates receives the abort signal as a parameter and passes it straight through to fetch, so the timeout policy is owned by the caller rather than decided here; a live model run may instead read the signal usage as resilience_present since the word 'signal' is textually present in the body, so this choice is recorded as the first live-run outcome rather than a certainty.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates regardless of the unguarded fetch inside it.
